Build a GDAL-style geotransform

Source: R/cb_affine.R
cb_geotransform.Rd

A geotransform is the six numbers c(x0, dx, rx, y0, ry, dy) that map a pixel position (col, row, counted from the top-left corner of the grid, 0-based) to world coordinates:

Usage

cb_geotransform(origin = c(0, 0), res = 1, rotation = 0, shear = 0)

Arguments

origin

Position of the top-left corner of the grid, c(x, y).

res

Cell size: one value, or c(width, height), in world units (positive).

rotation

Angle in degrees, counter-clockwise, of the direction in which columns increase, measured from the +x axis.

shear

Extra angle in degrees by which the direction in which rows increase is turned from being perpendicular to the columns (0 leaves the cells rectangular).

Value

A numeric vector of length 6 in GDAL order.

Details

x = x0 + col * dx + row * rx
y = y0 + col * ry + row * dy

This helper builds one from an origin, cell sizes, a rotation and a shear, so that rotated and sheared grids can be written down without doing the trigonometry by hand. A north-up grid is rotation = 0, shear = 0, which gives c(x0, res, 0, y0, 0, -res).

Examples

cb_geotransform(c(100, 200), res = 10)
#> [1] 100  10   0 200   0 -10
cb_geotransform(c(0, 0), res = c(2, 1), rotation = 30)
#> [1]  0.0000000  1.7320508  0.5000000  0.0000000  1.0000000 -0.8660254
